rules: Only confidence 'high' entries are used by scripts/build_creel_sites.py, and only after exact-name matching finds nothing. 'high' needs two independent signals. 'medium' entries are candidates for the owner to approve (change confidence to high) and are never applied. Every entry needs evidence. A ramp that WDFW counts boat and shore interviews at is attached to the map site at the same facility; the sheet keeps showing the source ramp name, so a pier site reads, for example, 'Kingston Public Ramp'.

evidence: Name: after dropping the generic words Ramp and Marina the source name is 'Boston Harbor', the whole name of the map site (WDFW access layer, concrete launch, Thurston County).
https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/218159023 : OSM slipway named 'Boston Harbor Boat Ramp', 42 m from the map site's coordinates (Overpass around 47.13966,-122.9055, 2026-10-18).

https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/18051670 : OSM marina 'Boston Harbor Marina' (https://www.bostonharbormarina.com/), 133 m from the map site; Nominatim gives its address as 312 73rd Avenue Northeast, Olympia, Thurston County.
WDFW catch area on every source row is Area 13, South Puget Sound, which is where this Thurston County ramp is.
entries.note: A ramp-and-marina facility; WDFW's one sampling unit is matched to the one launch site there.

evidence: Name: 'Brownsville Dock' is the map site's whole name; the source adds only '/Ramp'.

https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1053639712 and /node/9955748371 : OSM slipways 91 m and 95 m from the map site; https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/1053639716 : 'Port of Brownsville Marina' (https://www.portofbrownsville.org/), 126 m away, Kitsap County.
The map has exactly one site named 'Brownsville Dock' (Kitsap County), so the name is not shared.
entries.note: Pier-and-ramp pair at the Port of Brownsville: WDFW counts boat and shore interviews at the facility, so the counts describe the facility, not only the pier. The source also has 'Brownsville Marina' and 'Brownsville Marina/Dock/Ramp'; those are different WDFW names, were not sampled in 2026, and are not in this crosswalk. Last sampled 2026-07-24, so it shows nothing in the 30-day window.

evidence: Name: 'Cornet Bay' is the shared place name; the source adds Public Ramp, the map site adds Docks.

https://parks.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2023-07/Deception%20Pass%20Park%20Brochure.pdf : under Cornet Bay, 'Six-lane boat launch' and 'Mooring docks and nearby marine services' (pdftotext of the brochure, 2026-10-18).

https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1425057894 and neighbouring slipways: OSM boat ramps 105 m to 126 m from the map site; Overpass is_in puts the map site inside the OSM polygon 'Deception Pass State Park'.
entries.note: State-park launch and docks at one facility: WDFW counts boat and shore interviews there. The dropdown's separate 'Cornet Bay Marina' (OSM 'Deception Pass Marina', 381 m away) is a different WDFW name, was not sampled in 2026, and is not matched.

evidence: Name: 'Kingston Public' is identical once Ramp and Pier are dropped.

https://www.washingtonports.org/business-directory/port-of-kingston/ : the Port of Kingston lists 'Public boat launch/ramp, truck and trailer parking' and 'Recreational fishing pier' as one port's facilities.

OSM (Overpass 2026-10-18): the map site's coordinates are inside the OSM marina polygon 'Port of Kingston' (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3829217), and OSM 'Public Boat Launch' slipways (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2921322149) are 232 m from the pier.
entries.note: Ramp and pier are neighbouring parts of the Port of Kingston facility. WDFW counts boat and shore interviews at the facility, so the counts describe Kingston's public ramp and pier together; the sheet keeps the visible source name 'Kingston Public Ramp'.

evidence: https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/51361591 : OSM slipway 'Luhr Beach Boat Launch', operator Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, 56 m from the map site's coordinates.

https://nisquallyriver.org/watershed-services/recreation-opportunities/fishing-and-boating/ : lists 'Luhr's Landing' as 'Located at the Nisqually Reach Nature Center, the boat launch is open year round and permits motorized boats'; Luhr Beach and Luhr's Landing are one launch at the Nisqually Reach Nature Center (OSM: the same 56 m node).
WDFW catch areas on the source rows are Area 13, South Puget Sound and Nisqually River, both at this Thurston County site.
entries.note: The map also has 'Luhr's Beach Dock (CLOSED)' 80 m away. It is not used: the source ramp is the launch.

evidence: Name: 'Point Defiance Boathouse' equals the map site 'Point Defiance Marina Boathouse' once the generic word Marina is dropped.
https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/414285105 : OSM boat rental 'The Boat House', 32 m from the map site.

https://www.southsoundtalk.com/2026/06/15/boathouse-has-drawn-visitors-to-point-defiance-park-since-1903/ : the Boathouse 'forms the heart of Point Defiance Marina at Owen Beach' (Metro Parks Tacoma, Pierce County).
entries.note: WDFW counts boat and shore interviews at the boathouse and dock. The public launch ramp is a separate WDFW unit (Point Defiance Public Ramp) about 380 m away; see the medium entry.

entries.wdfw_ramp_name: Port of Friday Harbor Marina, San Juan Is
evidence: Name: 'Friday Harbor Marina' appears in both; the source adds Port of and the county, the map site adds Docks. The source name itself says San Juan Is and its main catch area is Area 7, San Juan Islands.
https://www.portfridayharbor.org/?p=2193 : 'The Port of Friday Harbor owns and operates the largest public marina in the San Juan Islands.'
https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/404795011 : OSM marina 'Port of Friday Harbor', 198 m from the map site, which sits 50 m from the marina's A Dock (way 4743201).
entries.note: Marina docks, not a launch ramp (the Port's launch is Jackson Beach, a different place). WDFW counts boat and shore interviews at the marina.

evidence: Name: 'Triton Cove' is the whole map name once the generic words State Park are dropped; it is the only Triton Cove site, in Jefferson County.
https://parks.wa.gov/find-parks/state-parks/triton-cove-state-park : 'a small day use park on Hood Canal', Brinnon WA 98320, with a boat ramp and ADA launch.

https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org (search 'Triton Cove State Park'): Jefferson County, 47.6086, -122.9900, about 700 m from the map site; the OSM slipway (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/3999766297) is 485 m from it. The source's only catch area is Area 12, Hood Canal.
entries.note: The map lists the launch as 'Hand launch' while the State Parks page lists a boat ramp; the map point is a few hundred metres from the OSM ramp inside the same small park. Distance is the weak point of this match.

evidence: Name: 'Twanoh' is the shared place name; both are the state park.

https://parks.wa.gov/find-parks/state-parks/twanoh-state-park : 'This park has one watercraft launch and 100 feet of dock', address 12190 E SR 106, Union WA 98592. The page does not use the word pier.

OSM (Overpass is_in, 2026-10-18): the map site's coordinates are inside the polygon 'Twanoh State Park' (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3740268), operator Washington State Parks; an OSM pier is 51 m from the site and the OSM slipway is 366 m away. The source's catch area is Area 12, Hood Canal.
entries.note: WDFW counts boat (launch) and shore (dock or pier) interviews at the park, so the counts describe Twanoh State Park as a whole; the sheet keeps the source name 'Twanoh State Park'.

evidence: Name: 'Point Defiance' only.

OSM slipways (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/4080920301) are 366 m to 399 m from the map site; Metro Parks Tacoma describes an 8-lane ramp next to the Vashon Ferry Terminal (https://www.parkstacoma.gov/boat-launch/, seen in a search summary; the page itself returned 403).
https://www.parkstacoma.gov/boat-launch/ : Parks Tacoma runs the Point Defiance public boat launch, 8 lanes beside the Vashon ferry terminal at Point Defiance Park.
https://www.visitpiercecounty.com/listing/point-defiance-marina/485/ : lists Point Defiance Marina, 5912 N Waterfront Dr, with 'Public launch' among its services (search excerpt).
https://www.waboatlaunches.com/point-defiance-park-boat-launch/ : gives the launch the same address, 5912 N Waterfront Dr.
entries.note: Approved 2026-10-18. The launch is a few hundred metres from the Boathouse dock (OSM slipways 366 to 399 m) at the same Point Defiance address. The sheet keeps showing the WDFW ramp name.

evidence: Name: 'Shilshole' only.

https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/679497545 : OSM slipway 'Eddie Vine Boat Ramp' (Seattle Parks), 37 m from the map site; Seattle describes Eddie Vine as the northernmost saltwater ramp, between Golden Gardens and Shilshole Marina (search summary of https://www.seattle.gov/parks/allparks/eddie-vine-boat-ramp). That Eddie Vine is WDFW's 'Shilshole Public Ramp' is an inference, not a page that says so.
The map also has 'Shilshole Marina (A-Dock)' 1.3 km south, so the name alone does not pick one.

https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/fishing-piers/shilshole-marina-pier : WDFW's Shilshole Marina Pier (Golden Gardens) page says the public fishing pier adjoins the public boat ramp at the north end of the marina facility (search excerpt).
https://www.seattle.gov/parks/parks/eddie-vine-boat-ramp : Seattle Parks names Eddie Vine as the city's northernmost saltwater boat ramp, between Golden Gardens park and Shilshole Marina.
https://www.waboatlaunches.com/shilshole-boat-launch/ : calls the Eddie Vine ramp the Shilshole Boat Launch.
entries.note: Approved 2026-10-18. WDFW's own pier page says the pier adjoins the public ramp, and Seattle Parks puts the only public ramp there as Eddie Vine. The separate Shilshole Marina (A-Dock) site stays unmatched. The sheet keeps showing the WDFW ramp name.

evidence: A search summary (Port of Everett grant news, https://pacificports.org/port-of-everett-awarded-1m-state-recreation-conservation-office-grant/) says the Norton Avenue launch is now the Jetty Landing and Boat Launch at 10th Street; the article fetched separately (https://www.liveineverett.com/blog//out-to-launch-where-to-get-your-boat-in-the-water) names the 10th Street Boat Launch but not Norton.
OSM slipway (https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2942900429) is 89 m from the map site 'Everett - 10th Street Marine Park Pier'.
No name in common between the source ramp and the map site.
https://www.portofeverett.com/news_detail_T31_R2303.php : the Port of Everett's own page names the Jetty Landing Boat Launch, 13 lanes, at 10th Street and West Marine View Drive.

https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/fishing-piers/everett-10th-street-marine-park-pier : WDFW describes the pier as 'Port of Everett: 10th Street Boat Launch and Marine Park' and links to that Port launch page, so WDFW puts the pier and the launch at one facility.

The Port of Everett's Facebook post (search excerpt, 2026-10-18) calls it 'The Norton Avenue Boat Launch (now Jetty Landing and Boat Launch)', which is the rename from WDFW's 'formerly Norton Street Ramp'.
entries.note: Approved 2026-10-18 on three independent signals. The Norton Avenue to Jetty Landing rename rests on the Port's Facebook post, not on a page on portofeverett.com; WDFW calls it Norton Street, the Port Norton Avenue. The sheet keeps showing the WDFW ramp name.
